edges.description: Photo-oxidative lysosomal injury can activate complement and chronic inflammatory responses through protein-adduct formation and impaired autophagic clearance.
RPE injury and disrupted cellular homeostasis impair support of the outer retina and contribute to photoreceptor degeneration and atrophy.
Chronic low-grade inflammation can exacerbate AMD tissue injury, although the complete set of intermediates leading to outer-retinal atrophy remains unresolved.

edges.description: Deposit accumulation precedes photoreceptor degeneration in the canonical AMD course, but the edge remains partial because drusen may also function as a biomarker and advanced AMD can occur without them.
Outer-retinal deposit accumulation is clinically observed as macular drusen.
Advanced outer-retinal atrophy in dry AMD is termed geographic atrophy.
Macular photoreceptor degeneration impairs central vision.
Outer-retinal dysfunction can reduce contrast sensitivity, particularly in intermediate AMD and under low-light conditions.
intermediate_mechanisms: impaired macular visual processing under low luminance

edges.description: Fragile macular neovascular complexes produce intraretinal thickening and subretinal exudation.
Neovascular wet AMD includes abnormal vessels arising from the choriocapillaris and presenting clinically as choroidal neovascularization.
Exudative disruption of macular architecture distorts central vision.
Exudative macular injury can produce a relative central scotoma.
Exudative damage to the macula reduces central vision.
intermediate_mechanisms: disruption of central retinal structure and function

edges.description: Variation in these genes is placed upstream of extracellular deposit accumulation because the FBLN5 carriers are defined clinically by cuticular drusen and the CST3 risk variant reduces secretion of a protease inhibitor into the same compartment. edges.description: Pointed at retinal pigment epithelium oxidative and lysosomal stress because that is where this entry places the earliest acquired injury, and oxidative stress is the route by which smoking is understood to reach it. Predisposing rather than triggering because the item is an incidence comparison between smokers and never-smokers, which is a statement about risk.

nodes.description: Variation in three genes whose products act on extracellular protein homeostasis at Bruch's membrane contributes to AMD susceptibility. Rare missense variants in FBLN5, a member of the fibulin gene family, were found only in AMD cases in a screen of five fibulin genes, and every carrier had cuticular drusen. CST3 encodes cystatin C, a cysteine proteinase inhibitor abundantly secreted by the retinal pigment epithelium and proposed to regulate protein turnover in Bruch's membrane; its AMD risk variant is secreted at reduced levels. TIMP3 is constitutively expressed by retinal pigment epithelium, resides in Bruch's membrane in healthy eyes where it regulates the membrane's thickness by inhibiting matrix metalloproteinases, and is implicated in AMD by rare coding variants. The node groups the three by the compartment they act in, and does not claim that they converge on one molecular step.
